q: What did Yahweh tell Moses to do with Aaron and his sons?
a: Yahweh told Moses to take Aaron and his sons, their special clothes and the anointing oil, the bull, two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread to the entrance to the tent of meeting.

q: What was the crown of holiness?
a: The holy crown was the golden flower-shaped plate fastened to the front of the turban.
Moses consecrated Aaron by pouring some of the oil of anointing on the head of Aaron.

q: Was an animal acceptable to eat if it only had a split hoof or if it only chewed the cud?
a: If an animal possessed only one of the two traits, it was not acceptable to eat.

q: What does Yahweh say about work and the Sabbath?
a: Yahweh says that people may work for six days, but the seventh day, the Sabbath, is to be a day of rest.

q: What must a man do with a field he has sanctified to Yahweh in the year of the jubilee?
a: When a man has sanctified a field to Yahweh and the year of the jubilee comes, the priest will figure the estimated value of the field up to the year of the jubilee and the man must pay its value on that day as a holy gift to Yahweh.

q: If a man redeems any of his tithe, what must he add to it?
a: If a man redeems any of his tithe, he must add a fifth to its value.
